div.head: I Cn Inscr.
div.ab: Ðis is seo gerednes, þe Cnut cyning, ealles Englalandes cyningc ⁊ Dena cyningc ⁊ Norþrigena cyningc, gerædde, ⁊ his witan, Gode to lofe ⁊ him sylfum to cynescipe ⁊ to þearfe, rade swa hwæðer swa man wille.

In nomine Domini. Ðis is seo gerædnes, þe witan geræddon ⁊ be manegum godum bisnum asmeadon; and þæt wæs geworden sona swa Cnút cyngc mid his witena geþeahte frið ⁊ freondscipe betweox Denum ⁊ Englum fullice gefæstnode ⁊ heora ærran saca ealle getwæmde.

Incipiunt quedam instituta de legibus regum Anglorum. (Inst. Cn.: Incipit lex que Anglice Danelage est uocata …; Cons. Cn.: Hec est consiliatio, quam Cnutus totius Anglie, Danorum et Nororum rex consiliatus est cum suis sapientibus apud Wintoniam …)

[Ðis is seo gerednes, þe Cnut cyning, ealles Englalandes cyningc ⁊ Dena cyningc ⁊ Norþrigena cyningc, gerædde, ⁊ his witan, Gode to lofe ⁊ him sylfum to cynescipe ⁊ to þearfe, rade swa hwæðer swa man wille.] [A]

(Inscr. Dies ist der Beschluss, welchen König Cnut von ganz England und Dänenkönig und Norwegerkönig beschloss, [er] und seine Witan, Gott zum Preise und sich selbst zur Königswürde und zu Nutze, bedenke man sich, was von beiden [ihn befolgen oder nicht] man will. A Cons.) (Im Namen des Herrn. Dies ist der Beschluss, welchen die Witan beschlossen und nach vielen guten Vorlagen ersannen; und dies ist geschehen, sobald als König Cnut mit Beirath seiner Witan Frieden und Freundschaft zwischen Dänen und Engländern vollständig befestigt und ihre früheren Streitsachen alle beigelegt hatte. D)

(Inscription. This is the ordinance which Cnut, king of all England and king of the Danes and king of the Norwegians, decreed, [he] and his witan, to the praise of God and to his own royal dignity and benefit; let each consider which of the two [to follow it or not] he will. A Cons.) (In the name of the Lord. This is the ordinance which the witan decided and devised after many good examples; and this was done as soon as King Cnut, with the counsel of his witan, had fully established peace and friendship between Danes and English and settled all their former disputes. D)

[This is the ordinance which King Canute, King of all England and of the Danes and the Norwegians, determined upon, together with his Councillors, to the praise of God and for the furtherance of his own royal authority and for his own benefit—let each man decide which course he will adopt.]

This is the ordinance which King Cnut, king of all England and king of the Danes and king of the Norwegians, and his councillors decreed, for the praise of God and for his own royal dignity and benefit; let one resolve whichever [course] one will.
div.note: Base text K = G (Cotton Nero A I, c. 1070, compared with Ld); N = A (Harley 55 f. 5, c. 1120); N3 = D (CCCC 201 p. 126, c. 1060, which contains only disordered and reworked fragments). O gives the Quadripartitus heading; the Instituta Cnuti and Consiliatio Cnuti headings are in brackets. A's heading is not original but is older than A. Dated 25 Dec. 1027–1034 (Christmas, Winchester).; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “Christmas, 1027–34; 1020/21 (Wormald); Winchester; 1020–23 (Whitelock)”, now “25 Dec. 1027–34 (Liebermann); 1020–23 (Whitelock); 1020/21 (Wormald); Winchester”)
This paragraph is only in the Harley MS.
If this were original, it would make the code later than Cnut’s victory over the Norwegians in 1030, or at least than his claims on Norway in 1027.
